body:
```py
>>> np.arange(4, 1, -1.2, dtype=np.int64)
array([4, 2, 0])
>>> cp.arange(4, 1, -1.2, dtype=cp.int64)
array([4, 3, 2])
```

```py
>>> np.arange(0, -4, -1.2, dtype=np.int64)
array([ 0, -1, -2, -3])
>>> np.arange(0.5, -4, -1.2, dtype=np.int64)
array([0, 0, 0, 0])
>>> np.arange(1, -4, -1.2, dtype=np.int64)
array([ 1,  0, -1, -2, -3])
>>> np.arange(2, -4, -1.2, dtype=np.int64)
array([ 2,  0, -2, -4, -6])
```

I think documenting this behavior is enough, as https://docs.scipy.org/doc/numpy/reference/generated/numpy.arange.html says
> When using a non-integer step, such as 0.1, the results will often not be consistent. It is better to use linspace for these cases.
title: cupy.arange behavior is inconsistent with numpy when non-integer step is specified
